changes: Device list, paired ids and sensory summary are stored as one server snapshot. Device change, removal and reconnect notifications coalesce into a scoped authenticated read instead of maintaining another partial list from push payloads.

Four lifecycle effects are consolidated into one request/subscription/timer owner. The socket hook must initialize before loading, so its initial null-to-socket transition does not duplicate the initial read; translation-object changes do not reload devices.

Account and active organization changes remount the view, and domain reconciliation blocks reads with an old authenticated organization. Logout aborts outstanding reads and writes and removes subscriptions and sensor listeners.

Pair and unpair share one button. Only one mutation is admitted at a time, explicit or incomplete rejection never becomes a locally invented pairing, and subsequent reads reconcile server state after each settled operation.
Device icon and translated label metadata share one table. Each device computes its paired flag once instead of repeated list lookups.
The newest memory-sync notification replaces the previous timer; unmount clears both sync and coalesced-refresh timers. Read failures show an inline error rather than an empty-list success.
validationNotes: Thirteen cases were added in the existing frontend behavior test file, covering authenticated read errors/retry, initial socket readiness, translation-only rerenders, three unconfirmed pairing responses, serialized pairing/unpairing, coalesced complete snapshots and timer cleanup, account/domain/logout transitions, and two late write outcomes after logout.

The first wider run had one test failure: AnimatePresence temporarily retains the old row during its exit animation. The assertion now waits for the real DOM removal; no animation or production behavior was changed to satisfy the test.

The event-burst fixture confirms that three notifications trigger one follow-up read and update device list, pairing and sensory summary together. This is a request-count check, not a real-device latency measurement.
Existing backend suites exercise device owner/domain authorization, real loopback HTTP/Socket.IO and test SQLite durability; UI fetches, account transitions and sensors remain synthetic.
limitations: Authoritative refresh replaces local event patching and adds a scoped GET after a device event burst or pairing attempt. Events are coalesced over 160 ms; there is no new polling loop or production performance benchmark.
The whole snapshot remains a full device list; this is not a database storage or whole-repository optimization completion claim.
Cancellation suppresses client continuations and cannot undo a server-accepted write. Concurrent pairing across multiple clients is still governed by the existing backend serialization.

The legacy system-access panel and backend broadcast recipient policy were not changed. In particular, Electron/native system-info capability and browser vault presentation still require separate review.
Business code decreases by 11 lines; tests increase by 95, making the total grow by 84. Earlier uncommitted work is preserved.
No full-suite run, actual device pairing, native-client acceptance, backend rebuild, user-data modification, commit, push or client restart.
